# Verification workflows

Guardian now defaults to Observations v2. The dedicated Guardian env can explicitly select legacy `LANGFUSE_READ_API=v1` where supported. The unchanged Founder exporter and manual workflow's 120-second poll window have not been verified against the modern source path; exporter compatibility and delayed availability must be resolved before treating a dispatch as a modern end-to-end acceptance check. See [source migration](../docs/SOURCE_MIGRATION.md).

`workflows/ci.yml` runs on pushes, pull requests and manual dispatch with read-only repository permissions and no application secrets. Guardian tests and synthetic-source localhost HTTP run on Python 3.11/3.13 across Linux/Windows. Founder dependencies/imports run in a separate Python 3.13 Linux job. Both React apps use Node 24/npm lockfiles for tests and production builds. Known product gaps are strict expected failures; unexpected passes require removing the marker with the actual fix.

The Python constraints record the locally resolved package versions, including transitive dependencies. They are not package-hash locks or vulnerability-audit evidence. Update each app's requirements and constraints together in an isolated environment, run `pip check`, then run the affected tests/builds. Review the hosted matrix before merging; local Windows evidence does not prove Linux or Python 3.11 behavior.

`workflows/live-verification.yml` only runs after manual dispatch with `allow_paid_test_traffic=true` on the repository default branch. It uses environment `guardian-verification`. Before adding credentials, configure that environment with required reviewers and a default-branch deployment restriction. Branch/environment protection is repository configuration, not something this file creates.

Add environment secrets `FOUNDER_VERIFY_ENV` and `GUARDIAN_VERIFY_ENV`, each containing the corresponding complete dedicated test environment file documented in [tools/README.md](../tools/README.md). Never paste production configuration. Both must assert `GUARDIAN_HARNESS_TEST_ONLY=1`, target the same dedicated Langfuse project, and use distinct Mongo names starting `guardian_verify_`; the Guardian database must have no collections. Choose a fresh Guardian database for each run and arrange test-data retention separately. The harness does not erase data.

Live dispatch authorizes one real Founder workload; retries/fallbacks may mean several paid provider calls. The workflow materializes credentials only for execution, removes its exact temporary files afterward and uploads only the sanitized JSON report. No report includes app logs or environment contents. It validates ingestion and HTTP; browser activation, source fault tolerance, organic incident detection, notification and recovery remain separate acceptance checks.

The workflows use reviewed commit-pinned GitHub actions. Maintain these pins deliberately when updating the runner/toolchain. The setup action's [Python executable output](https://github.com/actions/setup-python/blob/v7/action.yml) is passed explicitly to the subprocess harness. Hosted execution and environment setup have not yet been verified; see [VALIDATION.md](../docs/VALIDATION.md).
